events.objective: Establish the precise symptom onset timeline and blast radius for the order submit failures. Query logs and metrics to determine: (1) exactly when order-service error rate and 504s began (timestamp, to correlate against the v2.15.2 deploy time); (2) whether order-service itself shows internal errors/timeouts/throttling, or whether it is purely waiting on a downstream call; (3) which other services show elevated error rates or latency in the same window (list all, not just order-service); (4) resource trends (CPU, memory, connection pools, DB/gateway saturation) on order-service and its dependencies around onset. Report error signatures (exception types, status codes) distinguishing order-service-originated failures from propagated downstream failures.

Enumerate all changes and dependency structure relevant to order-service around the incident window. Using get_deployments and get_config_changes, list every deployment and config change across ALL services from 2026-03-17T06:00Z onward, including order-service v2.15.2 — with exact timestamps and whether each was a rollback, feature flag, infra/network change, or dependency version bump. Using get_service_dependencies, map order-service's upstream/downstream dependencies and identify shared components (databases, caches, queues, gateways, auth) that other affected services also use. Also run search_historical_incidents for prior order-submit 504/failure incidents and any prior incident tied to this same dependency or deploy-time pattern.

Correlate the change list from task b against the exact onset time and affected-service set from task a. Determine which change(s) either precede onset within a plausible window or are shared across all affected services; explicitly assess whether order-service v2.15.2 is causally consistent with the onset time and blast radius or whether a different change fits better. Also check for any rollback-relevant change: has a v2.15.2 rollback or any revert been deployed already, and did that change the error rate?

events.statement: Across ALL services in 2026-03-17T06:00Z–13:00Z there was exactly one deployment: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333), deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z by a.khan, summary "Add idempotency keys to order submit", already status "rolled_back" with rolled_back_at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z.

The deploy preceded the incident: release at 10:48:00Z, rollback at 11:16:00Z, report at 11:10:00Z — i.e. the rollback landed ~6 minutes after the incident was reported and ~28 min after deploy, and was NOT part of the reported trigger chain.

Across ALL services the only config change in the window was cfg-2290: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds changed 5 → 4 at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z by config-bot ("Shorter quote cache TTL") — no feature-flag, infra/network or dependency-version change appears.

No deployments and no config changes occurred in the 18 hours before the window (2026-03-16T12:00Z–2026-03-17T06:00Z): both queries returned count 0, so dep-5333 and cfg-2290 are the only changes anywhere near the onset.

order-service dependency structure: inbound edge api-gateway → order-service (http); outbound edges order-service → ledger-db (db), → pricing-engine (http), → exchange-gateway (http), → kafka (queue-produce); pricing-engine → market-data-service (http) and → redis-cache (cache); exchange-gateway → exchange-api (external, has_telemetry:false).

Shared components in order-service's path each serve multiple other services: ledger-db is shared:true and receives writes/reads from order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service; kafka is shared:true with order-service and payment-service producing and settlement-service and notification-service consuming. redis-cache is shared:true and sits behind pricing-engine; exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false.

Historical precedent set (leads only, not evidence): HIST-103 2025-10-21 "Order failures during exchange partner outage" (order-service + exchange-gateway, symptoms "504 on order submit", "upstream timeouts"); HIST-110 2026-01-15 ledger-db IOPS throttling causing order latency/statement timeouts; HIST-115 2025-09-25 order-service connection-pool misconfig ("pool exhausted") classified config_change; HIST-116 2025-12-18 api-gateway envoy upgrade causing "504 at gateway".

events.description: The historical-incident search for pricing-engine/quote-cache-TTL/deployment-regression patterns (targeting whether the 09:20Z pricing-engine cache TTL reduction has precedent) was not executed: the task's tool-call budget was exhausted before it ran.

No telemetry was queried in this task by design (change/dependency scope only); metric available_metrics for order-service, pricing-engine, ledger-db, kafka and redis-cache, and their behaviour around 09:20Z and 10:48Z, were not inspected.

Dependency queries were limited to ledger-db and kafka upstreams; who else reads redis-cache and exchange-gateway, and whether order-service's 30% failures coincide with degradation in payment-service/settlement-service/portfolio-service (the other ledger-db/kafka sharers), was not established.
No deployment/version history was found for exchange-api, whose has_telemetry:false flag means its behaviour is unobservable in this platform.

events.answer: Around the incident window the only deployment across all services was order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333, deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z, status "rolled_back" at 11:16:00Z, "Add idempotency keys to order submit"), and the only config change was pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4 at 09:20:00Z (cfg-2290). A 12h pre-window sweep (2026-03-16T12:00Z–2026-03-17T06:00Z) found zero deployments and zero config changes, so nothing older in the day explains the onset. order-service's dependency graph: api-gateway → order-service → {ledger-db (postgres, shared), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway → external exchange-api, kafka (shared queue)}; pricing-engine → market-data-service and redis-cache (shared). ledger-db and kafka each serve 4 services (portfolio/payment/settlement + order), so a shared-component fault would be expected to affect neighbours too. Historical leads: HIST-103 (504 on order submit from partner exchange outage) and HIST-110/HIST-115 (order-service vs ledger-db) — leads only, not evidence for this incident.

events.statement: order-service error_rate was flat ~0.16-0.23% through the 10:55 bucket (avg 0.21), then jumped to avg 19.02% (max 31.9) in the 11:00 bucket and stayed ~30-32% through 12:55. 5-min buckets, so true onset is between 10:55 and 11:05.

order-service logged 349 ERROR entries between 11:02:45Z and 12:58:54Z, with a single top pattern: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'. First occurrence 2026-03-17T11:02:45Z.

exchange-gateway is the origin of the failure signal: first upstream connect timeout to the external partner at 11:01:25Z (earlier than order-service's first 504 at 11:02:45Z), plus upstream 503s from exchange-api starting 11:02:20Z, and a circuit breaker opening for exchange-api at 11:03:26Z (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s). Patterns: 163x 'upstream connect timeout ... host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder', 146x 'op=quoteSnapshot', 161x 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable'.

exchange-gateway error_rate also jumped: flat ~0.17-0.23% through the 10:51 bucket, then 24.93% in the 10:58 bucket and ~43-45% sustained from 11:05 onward — a larger error rate than order-service's ~30%, consistent with order-service failing only the exchange-dependent subset of calls.

order-service latency_p99_ms jumped from ~149ms baseline (10:30-10:55 buckets) to 3264.85 avg in the 11:00 bucket and ~5300ms sustained from 11:05 — consistent with 504s timing out at the 5000ms exchange-gateway upstream timeout, not with internal slowness. CPU (~38-41%) and db_pool_in_use (~13.6-14.5 connections) on order-service stayed flat across onset, so no local resource saturation.

payment-service is NOT showing the same symptom: its error_rate stayed flat ~0.17-0.26% across the entire 10:30-12:57 window (no onset at 11:00), so the blast radius of the current window does not include payment-service at least in error rate.

events.answer: order-service's 504/error onset coincides with exchange-gateway losing its external partner (api.exchange-partner.example): first exchange-gateway upstream connect timeouts at 11:01:25Z, order-service error_rate jumping from ~0.2% (10:55 bucket) to 19.02% in the 11:00 bucket, and first order-service 504 log at 11:02:45Z. order-service itself shows no internal resource saturation (CPU flat ~40%, db_pool_in_use flat ~14, no restarts) — its failures are propagated downstream 504s from exchange-gateway. exchange-gateway error_rate rose to ~44%; payment-service error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% (no blast radius there so far).

args.query: rollback of deploy did not fix error rate
idempotency key order submit deploy errors

events.statement: The only change anywhere in the 06:00-13:00Z window is dep-5333: order-service v2.15.2, deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z, status 'rolled_back' with rolled_back_at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z. The second deployment query restricted to the post-rollback window 11:10-13:00Z returned count 0 deployments.

TIMING MISMATCH: dep-5333 deployed at 10:48:00Z, but the failure signal did not begin for another ~13 minutes -- first exchange-gateway upstream connect timeout at 11:01:25Z, order-service error_rate jumping in the 11:00 bucket (between 10:55 and 11:05), first order-service 504 at 11:02:45Z. During those first ~7 minutes after the deploy (10:48-10:55) order-service error_rate was still flat ~0.16-0.23%.

BLAST RADIUS MISMATCH: the origin of the failure signal is exchange-gateway -> external exchange-api (api.exchange-partner.example), and exchange-gateway is NOT shared ("shared":false) and is not a dependency of the deployed service's changed code path -- order-service only calls it for the exchange-dependent subset. exchange-gateway's error_rate (~44%) exceeds order-service's (~30%), consistent with order-service failing only a subset of calls.

Change graph of the deployed service: order-service's own downstream paths were untouched by dep-5333's scope (only the order-service submit handler changed); order-service's dependencies are ledger-db (shared:true), pricing-engine, exchange-gateway (shared:false), kafka (shared:true). exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false, so the failing hop has NO telemetry of its own.

The other in-window change, cfg-2290 (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5 -> 4 at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z), sits upstream of a different branch of order-service's graph (order-service -> pricing-engine -> market-data-service/redis-cache) and is >1h41m before onset; no config change exists on order-service itself (query scoped to order-service returned count 0).

Precedent leads (not evidence): HIST-111 (2025-05-22, category bad_deployment, ledger-db/settlement-service) and HIST-115 (2025-09-25, category config_change, order-service 'pool exhausted') both returned under the 'rollback did not fix error rate' query; the close-match incident for the current signature is HIST-103 2025-10-21 'Order failures during exchange partner outage' (order-service + exchange-gateway, '504 on order submit', 'upstream timeouts', root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', category dependency_failure).

events.description: No metric query was run for order-service error_rate specifically in the 11:16-13:00Z post-rollback period; the claim that the rollback changed/failed to change the error rate rests on the team's F8/F10/F11 series (error_rate still ~30-32% through 12:55) rather than an independent query by this agent.
get_deployments returned only a rolled_back_at field for dep-5333; no rollback deploy record, revert commit/PR id, or rollback event id exists in the deployment list (post-11:10 window count 0).

exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false, so no telemetry exists for the failing hop itself, and I ran no metric query on exchange-gateway's external endpoint health or on ledger-db/kafka/redis-cache saturation in this window.
Historical incident search returned only id/title/root_cause summaries (match_score-based), with no timeline of how long the rollback-blind precedents took to resolve.

events.answer: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333, deployed 10:48:00Z) is NOT causally consistent with the onset: the incident began 13 min later at 11:01:25Z (first exchange-gateway upstream connect timeout), originating on the exchange-gateway -> external exchange-api (api.exchange-partner.example) hop, which is outside the deployed service and is shared:false, so it explains neither the timing nor the blast radius. The change that fits is the external partner loss (HIST-103 pattern); the in-window pricing-engine TTL change (cfg-2290) is >100 min earlier and on a different path. On rollback: the deployment record reports status 'rolled_back' with rolled_back_at 11:16:00Z but a second query over 11:10-13:00Z shows count 0 deployments and no revert, and F8/F10/F11 show error rates still at ~30-32% (order-service) and ~43-45% (exchange-gateway) through 12:55-12:59 -- so the rollback did not change the error rate.

pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4 config change (cfg-2290) degrading the quote branch
exchange-gateway's own resource saturation / capacity limit causing upstream timeouts

tasks.answer: Around the incident window the only deployment across all services was order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333, deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z, status "rolled_back" at 11:16:00Z, "Add idempotency keys to order submit"), and the only config change was pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4 at 09:20:00Z (cfg-2290). A 12h pre-window sweep (2026-03-16T12:00Z–2026-03-17T06:00Z) found zero deployments and zero config changes, so nothing older in the day explains the onset. order-service's dependency graph: api-gateway → order-service → {ledger-db (postgres, shared), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway → external exchange-api, kafka (shared queue)}; pricing-engine → market-data-service and redis-cache (shared). ledger-db and kafka each serve 4 services (portfolio/payment/settlement + order), so a shared-component fault would be expected to affect neighbours too. Historical leads: HIST-103 (504 on order submit from partner exchange outage) and HIST-110/HIST-115 (order-service vs ledger-db) — leads only, not evidence for this incident.
